# CXNM - Standard - MAC - D - Login Window

Makes the login window ask for account name and password instead of showing a list of accounts, and shows a short message that the device is for authorised use only.

| | |
|---|---|
| Platform | macOS |
| Scope | Device (D) — assign to device groups |
| Type | Settings Catalog |
| Assignment | — |
| Source | CIS Apple macOS 26.0 Tahoe Benchmark v1.1.0 L1 2.11.3 (login banner) and 2.11.4 (prompt for name and password), mSCP branch tahoe; settingDefinitionIds verified against the settings catalog definitions |
| File | [`Baseline_MAC_D_Login_Window.json`](Baseline_MAC_D_Login_Window.json) |

> Banner text: "Alleen voor geautoriseerd gebruik. Activiteit op dit apparaat kan worden vastgelegd. / Authorized use only. Activity on this device may be logged." — generic, without an organisation name; adapt it to your own acceptable use policy (A.5.10) if that says something different. Maximum 1,032 characters. Overlap with CXNM - Standard - MAC - D - Accounts and Login checked: that one sets adminHostInfo, DisableConsoleAccess and HideAdminUsers in the same payload (com.apple.loginwindow); this policy sets SHOWFULLNAME and LoginwindowText. Different keys, no duplicate settingDefinitionId; macOS merges the keys from both profiles. Not put in Accounts and Login because that one comes from OpenIntuneBaseline and is in phase 1. The guest account is already off via Accounts and Login (DisableGuestAccount) and is not repeated here. Two CIS rules from the same section cannot be set via the settings catalog: 2.11.5 password hints (RetriesUntilHint) and 2.13.3 automatic login (com.apple.login.mcx.DisableAutoLoginClient) — the keys do not exist there. Automatic login is impossible anyway with FileVault on (FileVault policy). Platform SSO with enableCreateUserAtLogin actually works better with a name-and-password field: a new user types their Entra account there. SHOWFULLNAME overrides 'Show other users managed', which is not set.
